description:
Manage Settings

Update company configuration — the consolidated settings writer.

Actions (no ids — settings are singletons per company):
- offer_publish: make an offer public (id = offer UUID). First fetch
  type='offer_publication', then review its exact facts. Payload:
  {expected_version: preview.version, facts: preview.facts}. Owner/operator
  approval publishes these facts for buyers and agents, including discovery
  and incoming inquiries. Third-party copies cannot be recalled.
- offer_withdraw: make an offer private (id = offer UUID;
  payload = {expected_version}). Revokes its buyer sessions too.
- buyer_inquiry_decide: review a buyer inquiry (id = inquiry UUID;
  payload = {expected_version: action_version, decision: reply|decline,
  reply?: exact reviewed text}). Reply appears only in the buyer session.
- profile: update the company profile / ICP (`payload` = the profile
  fields; this steers research match scoring). If supplied, `industry`
  must be one CanonicalIndustry value: Agriculture, Construction,
  Consumer Goods, Consumer Services, Education, Energy & Utilities,
  Financial Services, Government, Healthcare, Hospitality & Travel,
  Legal Services, Manufacturing, Marketing & Advertising,
  Media & Entertainment, Nonprofit, Professional Services, Real Estate,
  Retail & E-commerce, Software & Technology, Staffing & Recruiting,
  Telecommunications, Transportation & Logistics, Wholesale & Distribution,
  or Other. Provider labels and Unspecified are rejected.
- auto_fill: AI-fill the company profile from the website (`payload`
  optional: {website_url?}; returns a job to poll via
  fetch type='job').
- automation: update workspace automation settings (`payload` = the
  automation fields, including the per-workspace diagnosis switch
  diagnosis_loop_disabled, and impact_verifier_default: who verifies
  customer impact on new promises, {roles, customer_confirmation_required};
  the role agent verifies only from the customer's own words and needs
  customer_confirmation_required=true and a human role beside it;
  owners and operators only).
- marketing: update LinkedIn marketing settings (`payload` = the
  marketing fields).
- cta_link: manage call-to-action links (`payload` = {action:
  create|update|delete, cta_link_id?, name?, url?, cta_type?,
  is_active?}).
- offer_create: add a live offer to the catalog objectives sell from
  (`payload` = {name, pricing_type?: fixed|commission|hybrid|custom,
  list_price_minor?, currency?, billing_period?, commission_rate_bps?,
  commission_basis?, pricing_notes?, description?, monetization_model?,
  contract_term_months?}).
  Fixed/hybrid require a minor-unit price (zero means free); commission/custom
  omit price and period. Commission rate may be unknown; a stated rate is
  1–10000 basis points (100 = 1%) and requires its revenue basis. Custom
  requires pricing_notes. Hybrid is a base fee plus commission.
  Monetary forecasts require fixed pricing or separate agreed deal terms.
  contract_term_months (1–120) is the declared contract term of a
  subscription or retainer offer, never its billing period: a 12-month
  contract billed monthly declares 12. The offer-term autopilot proposes
  one for a recurring offer that declares none; a term set here carries
  basis `operator` and no agent overwrites it.
- offer_update: edit a live offer (id = offer UUID; `payload` = {name?,
  description?, contract_term_months?}). Setting contract_term_months
  records basis `operator`; null clears the declaration so the autopilot
  may propose one again. Economic terms (price, currency, billing period,
  commission, monetization model) are immutable; retire and create a
  successor to change them.
- offer_retire: retire an offer no live objective sells (id = offer UUID;
  no payload); the name frees for a new live offer.
- view_save: save a private view of the Accounts, People or Deals table
  (`payload` = {tab: accounts|people|deals, name, definition: {params}}).
  params are the table's URL keys: accounts q, industry, account_list,
  research_objective, owner (me | member id), open_deals (yes|no), sort,
  dir, cols; people q, objective, research (researched|stub),
  account_list, list, stage, enrollment (enrolled|paused|stopped), score
  (60- | -39 | 40-59), added (7d|30d|90d|365d), persona, sort, dir, cols;
  deals q, scope, pipeline, stage (a stage label), owner, sort, dir,
  cols, mode (board; the table is the default).
  Returns the view with `url`, which opens it. When the caller can
  already see a view with the same filters (sort, dir, cols and mode
  aside), that view is returned with `reused: true` and nothing is
  saved. List views with fetch type='settings' subtype='record_views'
  filters={tab}. A new view is private and never pinned (each member
  pins their own); share it with view_update.
- view_update: rename, redefine, share or unshare a view the caller may
  change (id = view id; `payload` = {expected_revision, name?,
  definition?, shared?}). `shared: true` shows the view to everyone in
  the workspace; only the view's creator shares or unshares it.
- job_role_record: record a member's job role and ramp stage (`payload`
  = {role_key: sdr|ae|am|csm|marketer|founder|revops|other, ramp_stage:
  onboarding|ramping|established, user_id?, effective_from?}). The job
  role is what the person does, not their access (owner, member,
  operator); Vruum reads it to route suggested work to the person whose
  job fits. Omit user_id to record your own. An owner or operator may
  record anyone's: user_id is a member's user id from fetch
  type='settings' subtype='team_job_roles'. History is append-only, so a
  correction is a new record and the latest effective one is current.
  effective_from (ISO time the role began) defaults to now and is never
  in the future. The person's active coaching focuses made under a
  different role move to needs_review; the receipt returns the recorded
  `assignment`, the person's `current` job role and
  `focuses_needing_review`. Read your own with inspect_assistant
  practice_roles.
- work_hours_set: set YOUR OWN time zone, working days and hours
  (`payload` = {timezone?: IANA name such as America/New_York,
  working_days?: ISO weekdays, 1 = Monday to 7 = Sunday, work_start?,
  work_end?: HH:MM in that time zone, sent together}). Nobody sets them
  for someone else. The payload replaces what is stored: a field left
  out or null is cleared (the workspace's time zone, Monday to Friday,
  no stated hours), so send every value you want kept. The escalation
  clock for work routed to you counts your working days in your time
  zone. Hours are stored for the team to see; they do not change when
  anything sends.
- away_set: set a member's away dates and cover (`payload` = {user_id?,
  away_from?, away_until?: YYYY-MM-DD in the member's time zone, both
  ends included, sent together; cover_user_id?}). Omit user_id for
  yourself; an owner or operator may set anyone's. The payload replaces
  what is stored: both dates null ends the away period, cover_user_id
  null removes the cover. The cover is another member's user id from
  fetch type='settings' subtype='team_facts', never the Vruum agent.
  While a member is away, suggested work is not routed to them and an
  escalation reaches their cover instead (a cover who is away themself
  is not used). Being a cover gives no approval authority: who may
  approve what does not change.
- coverage_set: set the lists and accounts a member works (owners and
  operators only; `payload` = {user_id, coverage: [{kind: people_list |
  account_list | account, id}]}, at most 200). coverage is the WHOLE
  set: it replaces what is stored and [] clears it. ids are this
  workspace's people lists, account lists (both unarchived) or accounts
  (the account's company id); read the current set, with names, from
  fetch type='settings' subtype='team_facts'. Among members whose job role
  fits a piece of suggested work, the one whose coverage holds its
  account or person receives it. Coverage does not change who sends a
  message or who owns an account.
- account_owners_assign: assign account owners in bulk (owners and
  operators only; `payload` = {owner_user_id, scope: unowned | owned_by,
  account_list_id?, from_user_id?, limit?: 1-500, default 500}). scope
  'unowned' gives every unarchived account with no primary owner to
  owner_user_id, optionally only those in account_list_id; scope
  'owned_by' moves every account from_user_id owns. owner_user_id is a
  present member (fetch type='settings' subtype='team_facts'), never
  the Vruum agent. Each account gets what assigning its primary owner
  one at a time writes; an account whose owner changed after it was
  read is skipped, never overwritten. Returns {assigned, skipped,
  remaining}: call again while remaining is above zero. The account
  owner is accountable for suggested work on the account, so this
  changes who receives and may approve it. team_facts'
  `unowned_accounts` says how many accounts have no owner.
- hubspot_sync_settings: set the custom HubSpot contact properties to
  mirror into company_people.custom_fields (`payload` =
  {extra_contact_properties: [...]}); CHANGING the list auto-enqueues a
  full backfill so existing contacts pick up the new attributes.
- hubspot_backfill: kick a full HubSpot re-pull for this company (owners
  → companies → pipelines → contacts → deals → lists → engagements). No
  payload. Heavy (hours at 250k+ contacts). The recovery path when
  contacts were imported before their custom properties were configured.
  Operators target a client with `for_company`.
Team objective-delegation grant/revoke moved to manage_outreach
(objective_delegate / objective_revoke_delegation, VRU-878).

Payloads are validated by the underlying route's own schema, so a bad
field returns that route's precise 422.

### Responses:

**200**: Successful Response (Success Response)
Content-Type: application/json

action.description: The operation to perform — see the tool description for the action vocabulary and each action's id/payload semantics.
action.title: action

for_company.description: Optional company ID or name (UUID, or case-insensitive EXACT name match — partial / substring matches are NOT supported; ambiguous names raise 400) to execute this tool as. Use get_operator_companies, or get_operator_overview with view='companies', to list available companies. Only needed if you manage multiple companies. Access is enforced server-side: the tool resolves the value to a user_company_id and verifies the caller's membership in `company_users` — a 403 'Company not found or access denied' means EITHER the value did not match a known company OR the caller is not a member of it. The MCP operator role itself is NOT auto-granted — operators get this access by being members of each client company via `company_users` (the same row that grants any normal user access).
for_company.title: for_company

id.description: Target entity id, or an ARRAY of ids to apply the same action+payload to each (max 100; see the tool description for which entity the id names per action).
id.title: id

idempotency_key.description: Optional retry key, at most 255 characters; use a new UUID for each new action. An exact retry by the same caller within 24 hours replays the stored result. The same key with a different call is refused. After a failure whose outcome is unknown the key is refused: check current state, then use a new key. Actions that can preview or list always run and ignore it. Best effort: if the key store is unavailable the call runs unprotected. Payload request ids such as client_request_id still apply.
idempotency_key.title: idempotency_key

items.description: For create-like actions only: an array of per-item payloads processed in order with per-item results (max 100). Mutually exclusive with `id` and `payload`.
items.title: items

payload.description: Action-specific fields, validated by the underlying route. When the shape is unclear, fetch type=operation_contract with id='<tool>/action=<action>' for the exact nested schema; a tool-family id lists its operations. Reuse known contracts rather than fetching before every write.
payload.title: payload
